title: Optimized bio-harvesting method for Botryococcus braunii using Aspergillus sp.
author: Al-Hothaly

steps.title: Test fungal pellet formation
steps.instruction: Assess the ability of Aspergillus sp. (or other candidate fungi) to form pellets on solid and liquid media.

substeps.instruction: Prepare sterile Potato Dextrose Agar (PDA) and Potato Dextrose Broth (PDB) by dissolving 39 g of each medium in 1 L of RO water; bring to boil to ensure complete dissolution.
Autoclave the media at 121 °C for 15 min.
Cool sterile PDA to ~50 °C, add tetracycline to a final concentration of 0.015 g L⁻¹, mix gently, and pour 20 mL into each sterile Petri plate.
Inoculate each plate with 50–100 µL of Aspergillus sp. spores (from a 50 % glycerol stock) using a sterile spreader.
Incubate plates at 25–30 °C for up to 7 days until the mycelium covers most of the plate surface.
Sterilize a cork borer by dipping in 70 % ethanol, flaming, and allowing it to cool for 30–60 s; use it to punch 1 cm² plugs from the mycelial lawn.
Aseptically transfer up to five plugs into 100 mL of sterile PDB in 250 mL Erlenmeyer flasks.
Incubate flasks on an orbital shaker set to 28 °C and 150 rpm for up to 5 days.
Visually inspect cultures after 5 days for the formation of spherical fungal pellets.

steps.title: Test fungal growth in algal broth
steps.instruction: Verify that the selected fungus can grow and pelletise in the microalgal culture medium.

substeps.instruction: Culture Botryococcus braunii in BG11 medium for up to 4 days at 25 °C, 100 rpm, inoculating 500 mL BG11 with microalgae to a final concentration of 0.04 g L⁻¹.

Prepare BG11 medium (per litre) by adding: NaNO₃ 1.5 g, MgSO₄·7H₂O 0.075 g, CaCl₂·2H₂O 0.036 g, K₂HPO₄·3H₂O 0.040 g, C₆H₈FeNO₇ 0.006 g, C₆H₈O₇ 0.006 g, EDTA‑Na₂ 0.006 g; add trace elements: H₃BO₃ 0.00286 g, MnSO₄·H₂O 0.00181 g, ZnSO₄·7H₂O 0.000222 g, Na₂MoO₄·2H₂O 0.00039 g, CuSO₄·5H₂O 0.000079 g, Co(NO₃)₂·6H₂O 0.00049 g.
Incubate the inoculated BG11 flasks on a shaker with cool fluorescence illumination at 54 µmol m⁻² s⁻¹ for up to 4 days at 25 °C, 100 rpm.
Add 40 mL of the previously grown Aspergillus broth to 360 mL of the B. braunii broth using sterile 5 mL pipette tips.
Incubate the mixed cultures for 12 h at 25 °C, 100 rpm, under the same light intensity.
After 12 h, examine the cultures for (a) formation of ball‑like pellets and (b) disappearance or strong reduction of green algal colour; both observations indicate successful fungal‑algal co‑growth.

steps.title: Optimize fungal:algal ratio
steps.instruction: Determine the most efficient Aspergillus‑to‑B. braunii volume ratio for pellet formation in small‑scale trials.

substeps.instruction: Prepare B. braunii cultures as described in the previous step (BG11, 25 °C, 100 rpm).
Generate up to 1 L of fungal culture by inoculating PDB with either five 1 cm² plugs in 100 mL PDB or 100–200 µL of spores in 100 mL PDB; grow under the same conditions as above.
Set up the following fungal:algal volume ratios (fungal ml : algal ml): 1:1 (50:50), 1:10 (20:200), 1:20 (20:400), 1:30 (20:600), 1:40 (20:800), 1:50 (20:1000).
Add the calculated volume of fungal broth to the corresponding volume of algal broth for each ratio.
Prepare control flasks containing only algal broth (no fungus).
Allocate appropriate flask sizes: ratios 1 and 2 in 500 mL conical flasks; ratios 3 and 4 in 1000 mL flasks; ratios 5 and 6 in 2000 mL (2 L) flasks.
Place all flasks (treatments and controls) on a shaker at 25 °C, 150 rpm, with cool fluorescence light at 54 µmol m⁻² s⁻¹ (intensity may be increased up to 200 µmol m⁻² s⁻¹ if required).
Perform non‑destructive sampling at time 0 and every 4 or 6 h for a total of 120 h: aseptically withdraw 1–1.5 mL of culture supernatant into sterile 2 mL tubes.
Measure the optical density of each 1 mL sample at 680 nm and 750 nm using a spectrophotometer.
Record all OD values and plot OD versus time for each ratio to evaluate flocculation efficiency.

steps.title: Large‑scale bio‑harvesting
steps.instruction: Harvest B. braunii biomass from 250 L cultures using the optimal 1:40 fungal‑algal ratio.

substeps.instruction: Grow two B. braunii strains (K1 and O1) in 20 L batches as previously described (BG11, 25 °C, 100 rpm).
Prepare 30 L of modified BG11 broth for each strain using the same composition listed earlier.
Clean two 600 L circular fiberglass tanks with Milli‑Q water, then flush twice with sterile RO water.
Install multiple filtered air lines on each tank to supply aeration.
Add 490 L of sterile water to each tank, followed by 10 L of the prepared modified BG11 broth.
Introduce filtered air at a flow rate of ≥19 m³ min⁻¹ to ensure vigorous mixing; maintain continuous bubbling.

Cultivate the microalgae for 60 days under continuous aeration, illumination with cool fluorescence lamps at 54 µmol m⁻² s⁻¹ (intensity may be raised to 200 µmol m⁻² s⁻¹ as needed), and ambient temperature ≈25 °C.
Monitor air flow regularly and adjust to keep mixing consistent.
After 60 days, split each 500 L algal culture into two equal 250 L volumes.
Add Aspergillus sp. broth to each 250 L aliquot to achieve a 1:40 fungal:algal volume ratio; keep the paired 250 L aliquot as an untreated control (CTL).
For the treated 250 L batches, continue aeration and illumination at 54 µmol m⁻² s⁻¹ for an additional 12 h.
After 12 h, observe that the majority of algal cells have been incorporated into fungal pellets.
Harvest the pellets by draining the liquid through sieves of appropriate mesh size (selected based on pellet dimensions) to retain the pellets.
Collect the untreated control 250 L cultures and centrifuge them to obtain a comparable algal pellet fraction for downstream validation.

steps.title: Validate harvested biomass
steps.instruction: Confirm that fungal‑assisted harvesting does not alter the bioenergy properties of B. braunii biomass.

substeps.instruction: Subject harvested biomass from the fungal‑flocculated samples and the centrifuged control samples to analytical pyrolysis‑GC‑MS (Py‑GC‑MS) and preparative pyrolysis.

Compare the resulting bioenergy profiles; statistical analysis showed no significant difference (P ≥ 0.05), indicating that the harvesting method does not adversely affect downstream biofuel applications.
